dedupe_keys.name: boden type data centre one demonstration horizon 2020 sweden

description: This testbed and demonstration case is a prototype data centre built in Boden, northern Sweden, to show how far energy use and cost can be cut in a cold climate with renewable power. Funded by the EU Horizon 2020 programme and run from 2017 to about 2020 by a consortium of the Boden Business Agency, the Hungarian engineering firm H1 Systems, the British evaporative-cooling maker EcoCooling, Fraunhofer IOSB and RISE SICS North, the facility used direct fresh-air and evaporative cooling, controlled server fans together with facility fans to minimise airflow while keeping chip temperatures in range, and relied on the very stable hydro-powered local grid so that it could do without uninterruptible power supplies, batteries or generators. The project reported an annualised power usage effectiveness of 1.0148 and won a DCD award in 2019. Coverage: one prototype facility in Boden, Norrbotten. Format and access: free project news from the EU executive agency CINEA, a project presentation and the CORDIS project record with reports. Caveats: a small demonstration; the lack of backup power suits only exceptionally reliable grids; results were measured by the consortium. Simulation uses: design and optimisation of low-energy cooling, testing the resilience trade-off of removing backup power, and calibration of facility energy models. Related records: AlphaDataCenterCooling and SustainDC model cooling plants, and the Azure Australia East outage shows the risk of losing power to cooling.
